answer: A licensed lighthouse keeper watches a tower above the ocean, with a juniper grove as a windbreak. One tower per applicant for 120 days, with a 150 token deposit and a 90 dollar license. The keeper lights the lamp at dusk, logs flame and ships nightly, and a neighbor signs weekly. An inspector climbs twice to check lamp oil against the log. Forgery forfeits the deposit and bars the keeper 180 days. Faking 10,000 towers freezes 1,500,000 tokens and costs 900,000 dollars. A lighthouse only guides ships it lights, so a fake keeper stays dark and no ship follows a light that never burned.
